title: Privacy Policy
html:
Google Play · required URL

Privacy Policy

Effective 5 September 2026 · Applies to the Android app Goar (package app.goar) and this website.

Goar is a local app. There is no Goar server, no Goar account, and no Goar-run backend. The publisher of Goar does not operate a cloud service that receives your chats, files, or credentials.

Short version

  • Everything you type stays on this device unless you send it to a provider or server you choose.
  • API keys, SSH passwords, and similar secrets are stored on-device (encrypted when Android Keystore is available).
  • The app does not include analytics, crash telemetry, advertising SDKs, or automatic update checks.
  • This website sets no cookies and loads no third-party scripts or fonts.
  • Diagnostic capture in the app is off by default, stays in memory, and is never uploaded automatically.

Who is responsible

For data that never leaves your phone, you control it. For data you send to a third-party model, search, image, MCP, or SSH host, that operator’s privacy policy applies. Privacy questions about Goar itself: see Contact.

Information we collect

The publisher collects none. Goar does not create accounts, does not require an email, and does not phone home. Android cloud backup for the app is disabled.

On the device, Goar stores what you create: conversations, settings, API keys, SSH device records, notes, sandbox files, and optional exports. That store lives in app-private storage.

What leaves the device

Only when you use a feature you turned on:

  • Chat completions and model lists go to the AI provider you configured (for example OpenAI-compatible APIs, Groq, OpenRouter, a custom URL, or a local GGUF engine on the phone).
  • Web search, web fetch, image generation, and MCP calls go to the endpoints you enabled.
  • Installing the local sandbox downloads a Linux rootfs from the official Alpine (or Debian) distribution you selected.
  • SSH, SFTP, and VNC-over-SSH go to the host you pinned in Settings → Shell / Computer.

We do not see those requests. They are between your device and the service you named.

Permissions

  • Internet — to reach providers and hosts you configure.
  • Camera — optional, only if you attach a photo from the composer.
  • Notifications — optional local notices (tasks, overnight work). They do not leave the device.
  • Foreground service / boot — so long-running local jobs and scheduled tasks can continue while you use other apps.
  • Exact alarms — optional, for schedules you set. Off unless you use automation.
  • Legacy storage (Android 9 and below) — saving images to the gallery on old Android only.

Children

Goar is not directed at children under 13 and is not intended for use by children. We do not knowingly collect personal information from children. The Play store listing should be rated for a mature audience because the app can run shell commands and connect to arbitrary hosts you supply.

Your rights and deletion

There is no Goar account to delete. Uninstall the app to remove its private storage. In the app, Settings → Data control lets you export or erase conversations, memories, and settings. If you used a third-party provider, ask that provider about their deletion process.

Security

Secrets are stored on-device. SSH host keys are pinned after you trust them. VNC defaults to loopback on the remote machine; the app uses your SSH login as a pipe unless you change Computer settings. No method is perfect. You are responsible for the machines and keys you attach.

This website

These pages are static files. They do not set advertising or analytics cookies. Theme preference, if you toggle it, is stored in your browser’s localStorage only.

Changes

If a later build adds network features that send data to the publisher, this policy will be updated here and in the app (res/raw/privacy_policy.md). The date at the top is the current version.

Contact

Privacy requests: Contact or hello@goar.app.

title: Terms of Service
html:

Terms of Service

Effective 5 September 2026 · Android app Goar (app.goar).

By installing or using Goar, you agree to these terms. If you do not agree, do not use the app.

1. What Goar is

Goar is a local power tool, not a managed service. It can chat with models you configure, run tools, browse, edit files, and — if you enable them — execute shell commands, use an on-device Linux sandbox, or drive a remote desktop over SSH/VNC.

You are responsible for what the app does with the credentials and machines you give it, just as you are responsible for commands you type yourself.

2. Eligibility

You must be old enough to form a binding contract in your country, and at least 13 years of age. The app is not designed for children.

3. No Goar account

Goar has no built-in hosted model and no Goar account. There is nothing to subscribe to on our side. Purchase, if any, is through the store you used (Google Play or F-Droid).

4. Bring your own keys and hosts

  • Your use of third-party AI providers is governed by those providers’ terms and privacy policies.
  • If you connect SSH, VNC, MCP, search, or other infrastructure, you are responsible for that infrastructure, including lawful use and access rights.
  • Do not point Goar at systems you are not allowed to use.

5. Acceptable use

You will not use Goar to break the law, to attack systems you do not own or have permission to test, or to generate content that violates Google Play’s policies (including malware distribution, scams, or sexual content involving minors). The publisher may be required to remove the listing if the app is systematically abused; that does not create a monitoring duty on-device.

6. Licence to the software

The app is also offered under the MIT License (see License). These terms sit on top of that licence for store distribution. Third-party libraries keep their own licences.

7. No warranty

Goar is provided “as is,” without warranty of any kind, including merchantability, fitness for a particular purpose, and non-infringement. Remote desktops, sandboxes, and models can fail, hallucinate, or run destructive commands you approved.

8. Limitation of liability

To the maximum extent permitted by law, the authors and publisher of this software are not liable for damages arising from your use of Goar, including actions taken by models or tools you enable, data loss, or downtime on hosts you connected.

9. Store billing

If you download Goar from Google Play, Google’s terms and refund rules apply to that transaction. This site does not process payments.

10. Changes

We may update these terms when the app changes. The date above is the current version. Continued use after an update means you accept the new terms.

11. Contact

Contact or hello@goar.app.

title: Data safety
html:
Google Play Console

Data safety

Use this page when filling the Play Console Data safety form. It matches the F-Droid build: the publisher does not collect or share user data.

Play questionAnswer for Goar
Does the app collect or share user data?No data collected by the developer. No data shared by the developer.
AccountNo. There is no Goar account.
LocationNot collected.
Personal info (name, email)Not collected. Optional content you type stays on-device unless you send it to a provider you added.
Financial / paymentNot collected. Store billing, if any, is handled by Google Play.
Health / fitnessNot collected.
MessagesChat history is stored locally. It is not uploaded to a Goar server.
Photos / videos / filesProcessed on-device when you attach them. Not uploaded to the publisher.
AudioNot collected by the publisher. Optional camera capture is local.
App activity / diagnosticsNo analytics SDK. Optional in-app diagnostics stay in memory unless you export a file yourself.
Device IDs / advertising IDNot collected. No ads.
Data encrypted in transitTraffic to third parties you configure uses HTTPS or SSH. The publisher has no server to encrypt to.
Users can request deletionUninstall the app, or use Settings → Data control. No cloud account to erase.
Independent security reviewNo.
Committed to Play Families PolicyNo. Not designed for children.

Third parties you may enable

If you add an OpenAI-compatible key, a search API, Pollinations, an MCP URL, or an SSH host, those operators receive whatever you send them. Declare that in Play only if you ship a pre-wired key. This APK does not ship publisher-owned API keys. Default stills on Pollinations, if the user generates an image, go to that public endpoint — still not to a Goar backend.

Full policy: Privacy.

title: Contact
html:
Support · Play Console

Contact

Google Play requires a public way to reach the developer. There is no in-app account, so this page is the support URL. Email is the legal contact for privacy requests.

Email

hello@goar.app

Use the same address in Play Console → Developer account → Email address, and as the store listing support email.

Privacy requests

We do not hold a copy of your chats. To delete local data, uninstall Goar or use Settings → Data control. Email if you need that confirmed in writing.

No user accounts

Play’s “account deletion” requirement does not apply. There is no cloud profile to erase. Removing the app removes its private store.

Write to us

Opens your mail app. Nothing is posted to a Goar server.

Play Console copy

Paste these into the store listing. Short description (80 characters):

Private operator on your phone. Chat, files, terminal, live desktop. No account.

Full description:

Goar is a local operator for Android. Chat with models you configure, browse and edit files over SSH or an on-device Linux sandbox, run a terminal, and watch a live VNC desktop. There is no Goar account and no Goar server.

You bring API keys and hosts. Secrets stay on the device. The app does not include ads, analytics, or automatic update checks. Cloud backup is off.

Computer uses SSH only as a pipe to VNC on the machine you pin. Files, notes, and archives live in the Files destination. Creative image stills can use Pollinations without a key; video needs a key you supply.

Requires 64-bit ARM (arm64-v8a). Not for children. You are responsible for the systems and credentials you connect.

Privacy: the Privacy Policy URL on this site. Support: this page.
